newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil market quiet but unsure of week ahead.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil market quiet but unsure of week ahead.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets finished the week quietly on Friday amid uncertainty over the future direction of prices.
High sulphur barges started firmer, up at $83.50 from Thursday's last trade of $82.50. But they later slipped back amid poor bunker demand to be talked in a range of $82-$83.
"It's been a bit up and down today as if people didn't really quite know what to do," a trader said.
"People are asking themselves if it is the bottom or is it lower prices next week."
Some traders said it was not the time to trade from length.
"It's time to be cautious and stick close to the zero line," a dealer said.
High sulphur cargoes were discussed at slightly lower levels, $79-$81 cif, but no deals were heard done.
An end-April short covering to fill a cargo requirement for an Irish utility was said to have gone on Friday.
Low sulphur was again quiet and well supplied through into next month, with only active swaps play, at $88/$89 for April, giving any notion of physical prices.
One of the cargoes overhanging the market, belonging to a Belgian refiner, was heard traded to an Italian end-user on a quotes-related basis. - London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
